For me, cheats added some extra life to a video game after completing it; so I find it pretty disappointing that a lot of games are lacking them these days. There are a few games with cheats, but they just aren't that good. Take GTA: V for example, it has cheats, but they're really not that good in comparison to say, GTA: San Andreas.

Even CoD4 had cheats, but the newer games don't even bother with them anymore.

Does it take too much work to implement cheats? Do devs hate cheats? Or is just not worth it to implement cheat anymore?

What are your thoughts?
What's your opinion on cheats becoming non existent in recent video games?
I think cheats are a good way to squeeze some extra fun from the game once you are done playing it. Other than that, I don't see any reason why they should be implemented.

Some say that as many people do not have the time to complete a video game on their own, cheats are needed to make a game more accessible and appealing to a casual gamer.

Some what true.
I miss them. Part of the reason i replayed COD4 and Uncharted 2 so many times were the cheat codes. These days it seems like all we get are "new game+"

I understand why it doesn't happen in online gaming, like COD, but it should definitely be in single player. Having them is a good way to really get the full value of a game. I remember playing Tony Hawk Underground with my brothers for hours and using the cheats to keep things fresh and fun. I put hundreds of hours into it just because of the cheats. Also, local multiplayer should be mandatory on all games that have online multiplayer.

After a conversation in the comments of a post I thought some folks might have some questions. I quit almost 10 years ago (was a college job) and the firm I worked for was later bought and outsourced to Manilla, Fillipines.

Edit: figured I'd add that we worked by contract for a revolving door of clients that included movie studios, prescription drug makers and website owners mostly.
I'm a former paid internet marketer, AMA?

What does this involve? Social network promotions? Internet advertisements? Promotion on websites like this?

Do you get good pay?

Have any of the choices you have had to make regarding deceiving customers, made you feel ill?

What is your opinion on native advertising?

What ended your carrier?

1. There were a few different categories, mine was mostly pushing products on websites like this and Facebook in a subtle manner or via "expert" opinion or flat-out lying. I would post fake reviews for products on forums, I ran a MySpace for several movie "fan" pages that were created by the studios and made tons of reviews and recommendations for movies I've never seen. It was quite free-form, as long as it pushed my product/agenda and I could link to it for a random verification it pretty much flew.

  2. Nope, we worked as contractors and I averaged around minimum wage. They were very flexible though and you could work basically whenever you wanted as long as the shift wasn't over-full (only so many stations to use).

  3. All the time. We were pushed to flat-out lie when it was convenient and after awhile perpetuating so many lies that you have to keep notes can make you feel weird about yourself. It's kinda hard to explain but I imagine it's how a con man would feel after going legit.

  4. To me it's just a pop-up add or a commercial on TV. No real opinion either way I guess, it's there and trying to sell me something, just like everything else in life. I do feel bad for folks that lack critical thinking skills though and don't understand they are being duped.

  5. I took a job as a telemarketer, a switch which was widely considered as an upgrade LOL.
